_instructions: Give this file to your AI assistant (Claude, Cursor, etc) and ask it to analyze the codebase and generate project.json. The generated project.json should NOT be committed to git — add projects/*.json to .gitignore.
_prompt: Analyze this codebase and generate a filled project.json file based on the template below. To do this: read package.json, tsconfig.json, babel.config.js, README, and scan the full folder structure. Fill in every field based on what you actually find in the code — do not guess or leave placeholders. Be especially thorough with intentional_patterns (look for unusual or non-obvious code that could confuse a code reviewer who lacks project context) and review_rules (look for patterns the team enforces based on comments, existing code style, and linting config). For additional_context — think like a senior engineer joining the team: what would they need to know to review PRs correctly on this project?
name: Fill in: project name

languages: Fill in: e.g. TypeScript, Kotlin, Swift
frameworks: Fill in: e.g. React Native, Expo
key_libs: Fill in: library name — what it is used for and any important usage rules

structure:
Fill in: folder structure with the purpose of each folder. Example:
src/
  screens/   — screen-level components
  hooks/     — business logic
  services/  — API and DB
  utils/     — pure functions

import_aliases.Fill in alias e.g. @/: Fill in real path e.g. src/

intentional_patterns: Fill in: patterns that look like bugs or bad code but are intentional and correct. A code reviewer should NOT flag these. Look for: unusual data structures, non-standard async flows, empty stub methods, seemingly missing guards, unconventional patterns. Explain why each one is intentional.
review_rules:
Fill in: what matters most when reviewing PRs on this project. Format as:
- CRITICAL: things that must be fixed before merge
- IMPORTANT: things that should be fixed
- MINOR: style and quality improvements
- IGNORE: files or patterns to skip entirely (generated code, migrations, snapshots)

always_include.pattern: Fill in: regex pattern that matches file names in the diff e.g. wearTime
files: Fill in: files to automatically load as context when pattern matches e.g. src/utils/wearTime.ts

additional_context: Fill in: anything else specific to this project that would help a code reviewer understand the codebase correctly. Consider including: key business domain concepts and terminology, known technical debt areas to be aware of, performance-sensitive areas where changes need extra care, security-sensitive areas, important external service integrations and their quirks, non-obvious architectural decisions and why they were made, anything that requires domain knowledge to review a PR correctly.
